title: API: pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler at lib.rs:116 re-exports a foundation type unnecessarily
description:
lib.rs:116 declares 'pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;'.

What callers cannot depend on:
- The shape of ClosureHandler<B, C> (generic params, Send/Sync bounds, the BackendCallFn signature, the constructor parameter list) is owned by jmap-server, not by jmap-metadata-server. If jmap-server's next minor release reshapes ClosureHandler (e.g. adds a third generic param for a tracing span, or renames new() to with_backend()), this crate's public API silently breaks because the re-export carries the upstream shape verbatim.

Why the re-export is leaky:
- register_metadata_handlers() already does all the ClosureHandler wrapping internally via the reg! macro. A consumer of jmap-metadata-server never has to name ClosureHandler — they only need MetadataBackend and register_metadata_handlers.
- There is no example, no doctest, and no other reference to ClosureHandler anywhere in the metadata crate's docs or signatures that requires it to be publicly available from jmap_metadata_server::ClosureHandler. The only legitimate caller path is jmap_server::ClosureHandler directly.

Recommendation:
- Drop the re-export (delete lib.rs:116). Consumers who want ClosureHandler reach for it via 'use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;' — which they must already be doing for Dispatcher anyway.
- If the sibling canonical (jmap-mail-server) also re-exports ClosureHandler, this fix needs to be a canonical-template propagation: change the canonical first, then propagate to every extension-server sibling in the same pass per workspace AGENTS.md.

What goes wrong if this stays:
- Maintainability cost on every jmap-server release. The crate's apparent stability surface is bigger than its actual ownership.
